correctness.rationale: The period follows from \(M^4\equiv-I\pmod3\) and \(M^8=I+3A\) with unit entries in \(A\). For each singular branch the normalized difference has precisely the valuation of the index difference, because the higher binomial terms have at least one extra factor of three. This gives a bijection on every prime-power residue system. Square classes of \(3g\) are precisely \(g\equiv3s\pmod{3^{k-1}}\) for squares \(s\) modulo \(3^{k-2}\), yielding \(B_k\) and the full \(2\times2\) table. At infinite precision each singular branch is a geometric disjoint union of single cylinders of measure \(1/8\) with \(O(\log N)\) discrepancy. Standalone direct enumeration passed the first nine prime-power levels and 4,644 branch-difference tests; no infinite claim relies on those finite checks.

value.rationale: Simultaneous Fibonacci–Lucas square classes are a natural local analogue of their classical perfect-power and discriminant identities. The exact full four-cell spectrum at every three-power precision and the negative covariance are not inferable from individual sequence residue counts; the four normalized isometries identify the genuinely shared-index mechanism. The logarithmic error makes the limit effective. This is a meaningful complete local invariant, not an arbitrary small modulus table or a claim about global integer squares.
